user.title: JetBrains Junie Remote Authentication
user.description: Choose how to authenticate with JetBrains Junie Remote. Both choices require you to copy and paste session cookies from your browser; cookies are not captured automatically.

manual.title: Manual Cookie Input
manual.description:
Enter your session cookies from [Junie Remote](https://junie.jetbrains.com/remote/).

**How to find your cookies:**
1. Open [Junie Remote](https://junie.jetbrains.com/remote/) in your browser and sign in.
2. Open Developer Tools (F12 or Ctrl+Shift+I).
3. Go to the **Application** tab → **Cookies** → `junie.jetbrains.com`.
4. Copy the values for `SESSION` and `XSRF-TOKEN`.
5. Paste them as: `SESSION=your_session; XSRF-TOKEN=your_token`

**Required cookies:** `SESSION`, `XSRF-TOKEN` (and optionally `JBA`).

jba_oauth.title: JBA Web Login
jba_oauth.description: Sign in via [JetBrains Account Login]({login_url}) or [Junie Remote](https://junie.jetbrains.com/remote/) in your browser. Copy your session cookies (`SESSION` and `XSRF-TOKEN`) and paste them below.

storage.title: Transcript & Session Storage
storage.description:
Configure where session transcripts and state documents are saved.

**Security warning:** Home Assistant serves everything in `/config/www` at `/local/` without authentication. Earlier versions saved transcripts (prompts, source code and results) in `/config/www/junie_remote`; those copies are NOT deleted and may still be publicly readable and present in backups, so review and remove them yourself. New local transcripts are stored privately and served only to Home Assistant administrators. Paths inside `www` are rejected. S3 exposure depends on your bucket policy, CDN or public base URL, and presigned URLs are bearer credentials.

data.local_storage_path: Private local path (relative to /config/, must not be inside www)

3. Go to the **Application** tab → **Cookies** → `junie.jetbrains.com`.
4. Copy the values for `SESSION` and `XSRF-TOKEN`.
5. Paste them as: `SESSION=your_session; XSRF-TOKEN=your_token`
